messages.content: Help me add a 'click' event listener to a button element 'myButton' that triggers a function named 'handleButtonClick' and stops the event from propagating by setting options's stopProgation to true?

function.name: buttonAddClickHandler
function.description: This function attaches a click event listener to a specified button element with options to control event flow and behavior. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

element.description: The button element to which the event listener will be added. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

callback.description: The function to be called when the button is clicked. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

options.description: An options object to specify characteristics about the event listener, such as stopping propagation. Optional parameter. Default to be empty dictionary This is JavaScript dict type parameter in string representation.

message.reasoning: The user wants to add a click event listener to a button element 'myButton', with callback 'handleButtonClick', and options with stopPropagation set to true. The tool expects element and callback as strings representing JavaScript objects. So we need to pass element: "myButton" and callback: "handleButtonClick". Options: {stopPropagation:true}. But note the typo: stopProgation vs stopPropagation. The user wrote stopProgation. The tool expects options as string representation of a JavaScript dict. We should correct the typo? The user explicitly says "stopProgation to true". That seems like a mistake. The tool expects stopPropagation. We should correct it. The user might not realize the typo. We should correct it. So we pass options: "{stopPropagation:true}". Also note that the tool expects options as string representation of a JavaScript dict. So we pass options: "{stopPropagation:true}". The tool signature: element: string, callback: string, options?: string. So we call the function with element: "myButton", callback: "handleButtonClick", options: "{stopPropagation:true}".
